'''George F. Vande Woude Jr.''' (December 25, 1935 – April 13, 2021) was an American [[cancer researcher]], who, from 1999 to 2009,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=George F. Vande Woude, PhD |url=https://www.bcrf.org/researchers/george-f-vande-woude |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125100115/https://www.bcrf.org/researchers/george-f-vande-woude |archive-date=2021-01-25 |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[Breast Cancer Research Foundation]]}}</ref> served as the founding director of research at the [[Van Andel Institute]] (VAI).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Van Andel Institute's founding Director of Research, Dr. George Vande Woude, receives prestigious scientific award |url=https://www.vai.org/article/van-andel-institutes-founding-director-of-research-dr-george-vande-woude-receives-prestigious-scientific-award/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[Van Andel Institute]] |language=en}}</ref> He is credited with the 1984 discovery of [[MET (gene)|''MET'']],<ref name=":1" /> an [[oncogene]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=BCRF |date=2021-04-16 |title=BCRF Mourns Loss of Longtime Investigator Dr. George Vande Woude |url=https://www.bcrf.org/BCRF-Mourns-Loss-of-Dr-George-Vande-Woude |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=[[Breast Cancer Research Foundation]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life and education ==
George Vande Woude was born in [[Brooklyn]] on December 25, 1935, the son of Alice Leudesdorff Vande Woude and George F. Vande Woude Sr.<ref name=":2" /> 

George Jr. spent his early childhood living in [[Queens Village, Queens]]. He attended [[Hope College]] for a year before enlisting in the [[U.S. Army]]; during his service he was stationed in [[Baumholder]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=George F. Vande Woude Jr. | date=April 14, 2021 |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/name/george-vande-woude-obituary?pid=198340997 |access-date=2023-08-28 |publisher=[[Grand Rapids Press]] |language=en |via=Legacy.com}}</ref> Following his military service, he attended [[Hofstra University]], from where he received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jones |first=Peter A. |date=2021-06-01 |title=George F. Vande Woude: In Memoriam (1935–2021) |journal=Cancer Research |language=en |volume=81 |issue=11 |pages=2805–2806 |doi=10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-21-1345 |s2cid=235305088 |issn=0008-5472|doi-access=free }}</ref> He went on to receive a [[Master of Science]] degree in 1962 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1964, both from [[Rutgers University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2021-04-15 |title=In Memoriam: George Vande Woude, Ph.D. (1935-2021) |url=https://ccr.cancer.gov/news/article/in-memoriam-george-vande-woude-phd-1935-2021 |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[National Cancer Institute]] |language=en}}</ref> His degrees from Rutgers were in [[biochemistry]], with [[Academic minor|minors]] in [[physical chemistry]]; he researched under the laboratory of Frank F. Davis.<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vande Woude |first=George F. |title=Howard L. Bachrach |url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/bachrach_howard.pdf |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=[[Biographical Memoirs of the National Academy of Sciences|Biographical Memoirs]]}}</ref> He worked during college by driving a beer truck and operating a floor waxing business with his brother.<ref name=":5" />

While in Queens Village, he lived only a few blocks away from his future wife, Dorothy "Dot".{{Efn|In full: Dorothy Helen Vande Woude ({{nee|Stapel}}).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dorothy Vande Woude | date=August 2016 |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/name/dorothy-vande-woude-obituary?pid=180854637 |access-date=2023-08-28 |publisher=[[Grand Rapids Press]] |language=en |via=Legacy.com}}</ref>}}<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=VandeWoude |first1=Sue |last2=Vousden |first2=Karen H. |date=2021-12-07 |title=A celebration of the life of George Vande Woude |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=118 |issue=49 |doi=10.1073/pnas.2117952118 |pmid=34845037 |pmc=8670429 |bibcode=2021PNAS..11817952V |issn=0027-8424 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The two were married beginning on April 5, 1959, until her death in [[Belmont, Michigan]] on July 30, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dorothy "Dot" Helen Vande Woude |url=https://www.endersandshirley.com/obituary/5066641?lud=2548DFC3FAA94AECED0684044317B6F1 |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=Enders & Shirley Funeral Home |language=en}}</ref>

George died on April 13, 2021, aged 85, in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan]],{{Efn|His death place is also sometimes attributed as [[Belmont, Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Linda |date=April 24, 2021 |orig-date=Appeared in April 26, 2021 issue of ''Chemical & Engineering News'' |title=Obituary: George F. Vande Woude |url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-George-F-Vande-Woude/99/i15 |journal=Chemical & Engineering News |volume=99 |issue=15 |issn=0009-2347}}</ref>}} following a battle with [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
From 1964 to 1972, he worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral research associate]] and then a research [[virologist]] for the [[Plum Island Animal Disease Center]].<ref name=":0" /> He joined the [[National Cancer Institute]] (NCI) in 1972, serving as head of both the Human Tumor Studies and the Virus Tumor Biochemistry sections.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: George F. Vande Woude |url=https://www.aacr.org/professionals/membership/in-memoriam/george-f-vande-woude/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[American Association for Cancer Research]] |language=en}}</ref> Vande Woude worked in Building 41 at NCI until internal restructuring moved him to the [[Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research|NCI's branch in Frederick, Maryland]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Enquist |first=Lynn W. |date=2020-10-27 |editor-last=Sandri-Goldin |editor-first=Rozanne M. |title=Biographical Feature: The Long and Winding Road: My Career Path and How I Ended Up Where I Am Now |journal=Journal of Virology |language=en |volume=94 |issue=22 |doi=10.1128/JVI.01625-20 |issn=0022-538X |pmc=7592209 |pmid=32907976}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sherr |first=Charles J. |date=2018-03-04 |title=Pastimes in Cancer Biology |journal=Annual Review of Cancer Biology |language=en |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=1–19 |doi=10.1146/annurev-cancerbio-030617-050534 |s2cid=149295438 |issn=2472-3428|doi-access=free }}</ref>

His positions held within the NCI include head of the Human Tumor Studies and the Virus Tumor Biochemistry sections starting in 1972, chief of the Laboratory of Molecular Oncology starting 1980, and from 1983 until 1998 as director of the Advanced Bioscience Laboratories–Basic Research Program at Frederick.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2014 |title=Former NCI Researcher, George Vande Woude, Receives AAAS Fellowship Award |url=https://ncifrederick.cancer.gov/about/theposter/content/former-nci-researcher-george-vande-woude-receives-aaas-fellowship-award |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Poster |publisher=NCI at Frederick}}</ref>

He left the NCI to take the director position at the VAI in 1998.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Garber |first=Ken |date=2001-06-06 |title=Van Andel Institute Brings Cancer Research to the Heartland |url=https://academic.oup.com/jnci/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/jnci/93.11.803 |journal=Journal of the National Cancer Institute |language=en |volume=93 |issue=11 |pages=803–804 |doi=10.1093/jnci/93.11.803 |pmid=11390525 |issn=0027-8874|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He stepped down from his director position in 2009, but remained in leadership roles at the institute.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tunison |first=John |date=2021-04-13 |title=Van Andel Institute founding research director George Vande Woude dies, leaves lasting legacy |url=https://www.mlive.com/news/grand-rapids/2021/04/van-andel-institute-founding-research-director-george-vande-woude-dies-leaves-lasting-legacy.html |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=[[MLive]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Selected honors ==
{{Anchor|Honors}}
* 1981: Service on editorial board of ''[[Journal of Virology]]'' through 1987{{Efn|Service from 1981 through 1983,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=January 1981 |title=Front Matter |url=https://journals.asm.org/toc/jvi/37/1 |journal=Journal of Virology |volume=37 |issue=1}}</ref> 1984 through 1986,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=January 1984 |title=Front Matter |url=https://journals.asm.org/toc/jvi/49/1 |journal=Journal of Virology |volume=49 |issue=1}}</ref> and 1987 through 1989,<ref>{{Cite journal |date=January 1987 |title=Front Matter |url=https://journals.asm.org/toc/jvi/61/1 |journal=Journal of Virology |volume=61 |issue=1}}</ref> though he became an editor for 1988.}}
* 1988: Service as an editor of ''Journal of Virology'' through 1992<ref>{{Cite journal |date=January 1988 |title=Front Matter |url=https://journals.asm.org/toc/jvi/62/1 |journal=Journal of Virology |volume=62 |issue=1}}</ref>
* 1990: Sole founding editor-in-chief of ''[[Cell Growth & Differentiation]]''<ref>{{Cite web |title=History of AACR Publishing |url=https://www.aacr.org/about-the-aacr/history-of-aacr-publishing/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[American Association for Cancer Research]] |language=en}}</ref>
* 2006: Elected to the [[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=George F. Vande Woude |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/george-f-vande-woude |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] |date=July 27, 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
* 2007: Edition of [[Oncogene (journal)|''Oncogene'']] published in tribute<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Duesbery |first1=N. S. |last2=Teh |first2=B. T. |date=2007-02-01 |title=Cancer: biology and therapeutics – A tribute to George Vande Woude |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/6483270 |journal=Oncogene |language=en |volume=26 |issue=9 |pages=1258–1259 |doi=10.1038/sj.onc.1210257 |pmid=17322909 |s2cid=29791302 |issn=1476-5594|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* 2013: Elected to the inaugural class of [[List of fellows of the AACR Academy|Fellows of the AACR Academy]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Archives 2013 |url=https://www.aacr.org/professionals/membership/aacr-academy/fellows-class-year/2013/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=[[American Association for Cancer Research]] |page=10 |language=en}}</ref>
* 2015: Geoffrey Beene Builders of Science Award (with [[Jay Van Andel]]), conferred by Research!America<ref>{{Cite web |title=Science Award |url=https://geoffreybeenefoundation.com/science-award/ |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Geoffrey Beene Foundation}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-03-11 |title=2015 Research!America Advocacy Awards |url=https://www.researchamerica.org/additional-programming/2015-researchamerica-advocacy-awards/ |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=Research!America |language=en-US}}
*{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nWOdjVpxBR4 |title=George Vande Woude, PhD |date=2015-03-18 |publisher=ResearchAmerica |via=YouTube}}</ref>
